items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: Butter Beans and Susie used the show piano player.

ctx.x: opportunity to play was when the chorus girls...you know, you could really do your thing and play as hard as you wanted to which would be an inspiration to the chorus girls. But other than that they didn't have, you know, very seldom would you have a band that was the attraction. I can't even remember when they ever did that on the TOBA. And it's quite possible, but I'm telling you from my knowledge what they would do. They would...a guy would come on the show...he could play when the chorus girls were dancing,…

Clouds of Joy, Andy Kirk, you know, these guys were the Territory Bands that really, you know, played, but you very rarely saw Duke Ellington in Dallas, you know, during that period. He may play New York or Chicago or the Cotton Club or something and then go to California to Sebastian's or something like that. And then in 1927, when the Regal Theater opened, you know what I mean, they'd have a show. But they always had to have that original TOBA format of a comedian, Pigmeat Markham, you know what I mean,…
*Thomas A. Dorsey, then known as "Georgia Tom." Dorsey went on to compose the popular and well known Gospel hymn, "Precious Lord."
